--- title: Get the data description: Read OmicIDX Parquet from DuckDB, Python, or R over anonymous HTTPS. --- Every OmicIDX table is a Parquet file under `https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/`. Anything that reads Parquet over HTTPS can use it. You don't need an account or a key. There's no REST API. - **DuckDB:** [Query with DuckDB](duckdb-snapshot.qmd) covers the published database, every table, and example queries. - **R:** the [omicidxr](r-omicidxr.qmd) package connects in one line and replaces SRAdb and GEOmetadb. - **In the browser:** the [playground](../playground.qmd) runs SQL with DuckDB-Wasm, nothing to install. - **Pinning and citing:** [Versions and citation](versions-and-citation.qmd) explains `latest/`, dated folders, and the monthly HuggingFace releases. [Releases](../releases.qmd) lists what's available. The recipes below use `latest/` and ran when this page was built. Swap in `v{YYYY-MM-DD}/` to pin a date. ## Python With [polars](https://pola.rs), `scan_parquet` reads lazily, so only the columns and row groups a query needs are fetched. To try it without a project, run `uv run --with polars python`. ::: {.cell jupyter_compat='true'} ```{.python .cell-code} import polars as pl base = "https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest" studies = ( pl.scan_parquet(f"{base}/sradb/study.parquet") .filter(pl.col("study_type") == "Transcriptome Analysis") .select("study_accession", "study_title") .head(10) .collect() ) studies ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: With [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/docs/api/python/overview), attach the published database and get a polars frame back. `.pl()` needs [pyarrow](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/python/) installed, so run it with `uv run --with duckdb --with polars --with pyarrow python`: ::: {.cell jupyter_compat='true'} ```{.python .cell-code} import duckdb con = duckdb.connect() con.sql("ATTACH 'https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/omicidx.duckdb' AS omicidx (READ_ONLY)") gsms = con.sql("SELECT gsm FROM omicidx.geometadb.gse_gsm WHERE gse = 'GSE118849'").pl() gsms.head() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## R The [omicidxr](r-omicidxr.qmd) package connects for you, pins a version, and has SRAdb- and GEOmetadb-style helpers: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(omicidxr) con <- omicidx_connect() gsms <- geo_samples(con, "GSE118849") head(gsms[, c("gsm", "title", "gpl")]) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|gsm |title |gpl | |:----------|:-------------|:--------| |GSM3349109 |Exp #1-BAT-C |GPL17021 | |GSM3349110 |Exp #2-BAT-C |GPL17021 | |GSM3349111 |Exp #3-BAT-C |GPL17021 | |GSM3349112 |Exp #1-BAT-TN |GPL17021 | |GSM3349113 |Exp #2-BAT-TN |GPL17021 | |GSM3349114 |Exp #3-BAT-TN |GPL17021 |
::: ```{.r .cell-code} DBI::dbDisconnect(con) ``` ::: Without the package, [duckdb](https://r.duckdb.org) gives you the same database through DBI: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(DBI) con <- dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb()) dbExecute(con, "INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` #> [1] 0 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} dbExecute(con, "ATTACH 'https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/omicidx.duckdb' AS omicidx (READ_ONLY)") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` #> [1] 0 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} gsms <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT gsm FROM omicidx.geometadb.gse_gsm WHERE gse = 'GSE118849'") # Any table, without the database dbGetQuery(con, " SELECT count(*) AS n FROM read_parquet('https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/sra_studies.parquet') ") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}

::: ```{.r .cell-code} dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE) ``` ::: ## Command line ```bash # Row counts for every published table curl -s https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/manifest.json # One table, downloaded curl -O https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/geometadb/gse.parquet ```
